# NO — you are NOT paying for AT SIP trunk.

Hard checks I just ran:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `SIP_*` / `TRUNK_*` env vars in Vercel | **None** |
| `.env.local` SIP config | **None** |
| Any SIP-related code in curriculum-app | **None** |
| AT_USERNAME / AT_API_KEY (current creds) | These are for the **HTTP Voice API**, not SIP |

What you're currently paying for at AT is:
- The production phone number **+2342017001459** (the ~$185 one-time you paid)
- Per-minute inbound voice on the **HTTP webhook API** (~₦3/min)
- Wallet balance for outbound SMS

**AT SIP trunking is a completely separate product** — it requires:
- Your own SIP-capable client (Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, a softphone, or browser WebRTC)
- A separate sign-up flow + KYC
- Different credentials (SIP username/password, not API key)
- Different per-min rate ($0.0040/min on their newer SIP product per my research notes)

You'd see it as a distinct line in your AT billing dashboard if it were active. It isn't, because we never configured it. Want me to check your AT dashboard config remotely (I'd need you to give me an active session) or do you want to just look yourself at `account.africastalking.com` → Voice → SIP?

## Why The SIP Question Matters Right Now

If you're considering SIP trunk as the fix for the "AT doesn't do live back-and-forth" problem we just hit — **that's actually the right instinct.** SIP IS the path to real-time interactive voice. With SIP:

- You connect a media server (Asterisk / FreeSWITCH / Jambonz) directly to AT's voice network
- Audio streams **bidirectionally in real-time** — no "record-then-callback" async pattern
- Your server can play TTS + capture STT in the same call, no XML callbacks needed
- That's what would unlock kid-says-something → Sabi-responds-instantly → kid-says-more in ONE call

But it's a bigger architectural lift than the current HTTP webhook setup. Roughly: you'd run a small Jambonz or Asterisk instance somewhere (~$10-30/mo VPS), point AT's SIP trunk at it, and replace the `/api/sabi/at/*` routes with WebSocket-based audio streaming.

Worth doing for the pilot if interactive matters more than launch speed. **Want me to scope what that switch would look like?**

Sources:
- [Africa's Talking SIP Documentation](https://developers.africastalking.com/docs/voice/SIP)
- [Africa's Talking SIP Trunking Help](https://help.africastalking.com/en/articles/2189469-what-is-sip-trunking)

# Clearing The Air — Then SIP Pricing

## What you actually paid

Looking back at your statement: **₦5,000 = ~$3 USD**. That's a wallet top-up for usage, NOT a production-number purchase fee.

The "~$185–195" figure I'd been working from must have been the QUOTED price for the production number, which you said you **haven't paid yet.** This matters: if the production number is still in trial / pending-activation state on AT's side, that could partially explain why call behavior has been weird (capped features, sandboxed flows, etc.).

**Action: when you call AT support, ask directly — "Is +2342017001459 a fully-paid production number, or still on a trial / activation hold?"** They'll tell you immediately.

## What AT's SIP costs (best I can pull from their public pages)

AT hides actual Nigeria pricing behind a PDF and login wall, so this is partial. Cross-referencing what I could find:

| Item | AT SIP rate (where I could see it) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SIP-to-SIP call | ~1 unit/min (~₦1–2/min Nigeria) | Two SIP endpoints talking to each other |
| SIP-to-PSTN (real phone) | ~5 units/min (~₦5/min Nigeria) | Your server SIP → kid's mobile |
| SIP-to-virtual-number | Same as PSTN-equivalent | When someone dials your AT-hosted number → routes via SIP to your server |
| Virtual number monthly fee | Not publicly listed | Likely $5–25/month — ask support |
| Production number purchase | The amount you mentioned (~$195) | Per their quote — **one-time fee, not yet paid by you** |

These numbers are approximate because AT genuinely doesn't publish Nigerian voice rates publicly. **The AT customer support number is the right way to get exact figures + your account status.**

## What "the plan" was — original strategy

The original architecture I'd been building toward:

1. **AT virtual number** for inbound (where Nigerian kids dial in cheaply at local rates)
2. **AT HTTP webhook** for handling calls (REST/XML responses — what we have now)
3. **Self-hosted Sabi backend** (Vercel) processes the audio
4. **AT SMS** for follow-up practice questions

**That plan does NOT include SIP.** Everything is HTTP webhooks.

**The SIP question only matters NOW because** we just discovered AT's HTTP webhook doesn't support live in-call back-and-forth recording — it delivers recordings async via the `/events` callback after the call ends. That's a hard limit of their HTTP API. SIP IS their interactive-voice path.

## Decision Tree When You Call Support

Ask them three things in order:

1. **"Is my production number +2342017001459 fully paid and activated, or still in trial?"**
2. **"Can your HTTP Voice API do live in-call recording → server response → continued conversation in one call, or do I need SIP trunking for that?"**
3. **"What's the actual SIP trunk cost for Nigeria — setup, monthly, per-minute?"**

Their answers determine whether we:
- (A) Stay on HTTP webhook + accept async UX (cheap, current code mostly works)
- (B) Pay for SIP trunk + rebuild for real-time interactive (more expensive, but the real product)
- (C) Switch providers entirely

Call them. **AT customer support: +254-20-2335018 (Nairobi HQ) or +234-908-739-3909 (Nigeria).** Email: voice@africastalking.com. Want me to also keep the current async pipeline polished so option A is a working fallback whatever they say?

Sources:
- [Africa's Talking SIP Documentation](https://developers.africastalking.com/docs/voice/SIP)
- [How do I set up SIP trunk connection](https://help.africastalking.com/en/articles/6049012-what-do-i-need-to-set-up-a-sip-trunk-connection)
- [Voice pricing Nigeria help](https://help.africastalking.com/en/articles/12318772-consolidated-voice-pricing)
- [How AT voice billing works](https://help.africastalking.com/en/articles/1152209-how-does-voice-billing-work)

Voice

Build dynamic, scalable, fully-featured voice applications that operate entirely in the cloud, eliminating the need to invest in and maintain costly voice equipment. This reduces your business costs while increasing the efficiency of how you reach your users.
Some possible use cases
Call centers (Remote and Physical): Manage calls, support, and agent efficiency.
User authentication (Two-Factor Authentication): Secure OTP via voice.
Call Blasting/Robocalls: Broadcast audio messages efficiently.
Surveys: Gather valuable feedback through automated voice surveys.
How it works

Below is an illustration on how the Voice service works
Voice API illustration
Once your account setup is complete, you’ll need to:
Register a Phone number with us.
Register a callback URL, ensure that this URL is valid and accessible, allowing us to send requests to it.
To initiate a call from your application, send a POST request to our Voice API. Upon call connection, we’ll notify your callback URL, allowing your application to dictate call handling.
Subsequent actions hinge on the response received from your application. If user input is needed, we’ll send another notification to your callback URL to gather the input and determine the next steps. This iterative process continues until either the user ends the call or your application specifies an action to conclude it.
Upon call termination, we’ll send a final notification to your callback URL, furnishing additional details like call cost and duration.

Calling Out

Make an outbound call through our Voice API by sending a HTTP POST request to our endpoint:
Endpoints
Live: https://voice.africastalking.com/call
Request Parameters

In addition to the standard request headers, the request should contain the following fields:
Parameter	Location	Description
Content-Type
Required	Header	The requests content type. Can be application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data
username
String
Required	Body	Your Africa’s Talking application username
from
String
Required	Body	Your Africa’s Talking phone number (in international format i.e. +XXXYYYYYY)
to
String
Required	Body	A comma separated string of recipients’ phone numbers.
clientRequestId
String
Optional	Body	Variable sent to your Events Callback URL that can be used to tag the call
API Response

The body of the response will be a XML object containing the following fields:
Parameter	Description
entries
List	A list with multiple Entry each corresponding to an individual phone number and their status. Entry is a Map with details of queued numbers.
phoneNumber: String The phone number queued.
status: String The status of the request associated to this phone number. Possible values are:
Queued: The call request has been accepted and queued
InvalidPhoneNumber: Recipient number is in an incorrect format
DestinationNotSupported: Recipient number is outside the supported zone
InsufficientCredit: Your AfricasTalking account has insufficient balance.
sessionId: String A unique id for the request associated to this phone number. Defaults to None if an error occurred.
errorMessage
String
Optional	Error message if the ENTIRE request was rejected by the API.
On top of the regular response header, the following special field will be returned:
Parameter	Description
X-Current-Queue-Size	A HTTP Header header indicating the number of queued calls at the time of request

Copy
curl -X POST \
    https://voice.africastalking.com/call \
    -H 'Accept: application/json' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
    -H 'apiKey: [REDACTED:header-credential]' \
    -d 'username=myAppUserName&to=%5B%2B24572301837%2C%20%2B2546371910283%5D&from=%2B2549284789292'
Example Response
{
    "entries": [
        {
            "phoneNumber": "+234XXXYYYZZZZ",
            "status": "Queued",
            "sessionId": "ATVId_abcdef"
        }
    ],
    "errorMessage": "None"
}

Handling a Call Session

Handling voice calls made to and from your Africa’s Talking phone number is as easy as implementing a script on your web server that handles HTTP POST requests.
Steps Involved In Handling A Call Session

Here is how it all comes together…
We receive a call to your phone number on our voice gateways, or you successfully initiate a call using our calling API
Our API sends a POST request to the notification callback URL that you have set for that phone number in your Voice Dashboard.
Your application responds with XML that tells our API how to handle the call. This XML will typically contain a list of actions that our API will execute in sequence.
Our API translates those actions into events or messages relayed back to the caller.
POST Payload Sent From Our APIs

The post request that we submit to your callback URL will contain the following fields:
Field	Description	Presence
isActive	This lets your application know the call session state. The API will set a value of 0in the final request to your application. The value is 1 for an ongoing call.	All requests
sessionId	This is a unique identifier that we will generate during each call session. This field will stay the same throughout the call session	All requests
direction	Whether this is an inbound or outbound call. Inbound calls are initiated by a phone user while outbound calls are initiated by your application.	All requests
callerNumber	The phone number of the phone user in the call. The phone numbers are all in international format (such as +254711XXXYYY)	All requests
destinationNumber	Your Africa’s Talking phone number. This will also be presented in international format, starting with a +.	All requests
dtmfDigits	This variable contains the digits that a user enters in response to a < GetDigits /> request	Request following a GetDigits response
recordingUrl	The URL of the recording made for this call (using either the Record element, or the record attribute of the Bridge element	Final Request
durationInSeconds	The duration of the call in seconds.	Final Request
currencyCode	The currency used to bill this call (e.g KES, USD, GBP).	Final Request
amount	The total cost of the call.	Final Request

Call Transfer

You can transfer your call to another number by making a HTTP POST request to one of the following endpoints:
Endpoints
Live: https://voice.africastalking.com/callTransfer
Request payload

In addition to the standard request headers, the body of the request should contain the following fields:
Field	Description
sessionId
String
Required	Session Id of the ongoing call, it must have two legs
phoneNumber
String
Required	Phone Number to transfer the call to
callLeg
String
Optional	Call leg to transfer the call to either caller or callee(Defaults to callee)
holdMusicUrl
String
Optional	The url of the media file to be played when the user is on hold. Don’t forget to start with http://
API Response

The body of the response will be an XML object containing the following fields:
Field	Description
status	can be either Success or Aborted
errorMessage	Why the transfer ws aborted None is successful
Below is a sample make call response for a successful request:
<callTransferResponse>
    <status>Success</status>
    <errorMessage>None</errorMessage>
</callTransferResponse>
Event Notifications

When the transfer has been initiated we will send any of these events to your event notifications URL, you can check from these form fields in the events:
Event	Fields
Call transferred but failed	
callSessionState = Active
isActive = 1
callTransferHangupCause = {{ DestinationNotSupported, InvalidPhoneNumber, NoActiveClient, NotAllowed }}
Call successfully transferred	
callSessionState = Transferred
isActive = 1
callTransferredToNumber = {{ number call was transferred to }}
callTransferState = Active
Call transfer ends	
callSessionState = TransferCompleted
isActive = 1
callTransferredToNumber = {{ number call was transferred to }}
callTransferState = Completed
Caller hangsup	
callSessionState = Active
isActive = 1
callTransferState = CallerHangup
Callee hangup	
callSessionState = Active
isActive = 1
callTransferState = CalleeHangup
End of call	
callTransferParam = +2347XXXXXXXXX:20, (20 is the duration in seconds)
status = Success
callSessionState = Completed
isActive = 0
Call is transferred on the callee leg

When the call transfer is active then you can execute this DTMF on the callee leg
DTMF Digit	Description
0	Convert the call to a three-way conference after the last party answers the call
*	Hangup the the callee leg and return the caller to the transferred phone number
#	Hangup the transferred phone number and return the callee to the caller
Call is transferred on the caller leg

When the call transfer is active then you can execute this DTMF on the caller leg
DTMF Digit	Description
0	Convert the call to a three-way conference after the last party answers the call
*	Hangup the the caller leg and return the callee to the transferred phone number
#	Hangup the transferred phone number and return the caller to the callee

Voice Actions

A voice action is what your application sends in response to a notification that tells the Voice API how to handle the current call.
Action	Description
Say	With this action, you set a text and we will read it out to the caller (text to speech).
Play	This element lets you play back a static audio file that is located anywhere on the web.
Get Digits	You can use this element to get the digits that a user enters on their phone in response to a prompt from your application.
Dial	You can use this action to connect your calls to an agent connected on WebRTC, Sip phone or external phone number(s).
Record	This element lets you record a call session into an mp3 file that you can then retrieve and play later. Our API supports terminal recording or partial recording. For final recording, the recording starts when the record action is called until the mobile user hangs up. Partial recording may be useful where a particular user response is required like while prompting for a name.
Enqueue	Lets you pass an incoming call to a queue to be handled later.
Dequeue	Lets you pass the calls enqueued to a separate number so that it can be handled e.g by an agent.
Redirect	This action will transfer control of the call to the script whose URL is passed in. This can help you better organize your call handling logic by spreading the logic across multiple scripts.
Reject	This action lets you conditionally reject calls.
Conference	This action lets you create call conference rooms and dynamically control the room and its participants
Note
Any action that takes input from the user such as [Get Digits](/docs/voice/actions/getdigits) and [Record](/docs/voice/actions/record) will trigger another notification to your application with those values so we can know what next action to take. This is so that you can perform some logic depending on the user's input.
Input Prompts

You can nest either a Say element or Play element inside a GetDigits or Record element. This will be used to prompt the user.
Here is a sample GetDigit response, with a Say prompt:
<Response>
    <GetDigits timeout="30" finishOnKey="#">
        <Say>Please enter your account number followed by the hash sign</Say>
    </GetDigits>
</Response>
Here is a sample Record response with a play prompt:
<Response>
    <Record finishOnKey="#" maxLength="10" trimSilence="true" playBeep="true">
        <Play url="http://www.myvoicemailserver.com/audio/vmail.wav"/>
    </Record>
</Response>

Say (Text-to-Speech)

You can send us some text (in any google TTS supported language) and we will read it out to the user. For example, let us say we want to tell the user what their account balance is. Your web server can respond to our request with the following XML:
<Response>
    <Say voice="en-US-Standard-C" playBeep="false" >Your balance is 1234 Shillings</Say>
</Response>
The Say element can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
voice
Optional	This attribute specifies the voice to use. You can get the possible list of values on Google’s Text-to-Speech supported voices here.
playBeep
Optional	This attribute instructs our API to play a beep after reading the text contained in the request. The possible values are true and false (default: false)
Synthesized Speech Attributes.

The Say action supports the use of Speech Synthesis Markup Language(SSML). The root tag for SSML starts with <speak> as shown below:
<Response>
    <Say voice= "en-US-Wavenet-C">
      <speak>My speech content.</speak>
    </Say>
</Response>
You can pass the following tag within the <speak> to control the generated synthesized speech.
1. <break>

Controls pausing or other prosodic boundaries between words. By default, the break is automatically determined based on the linguistic context. It can take the following attributes:
Attribute	Description
time
Optional	Sets the length of the break by seconds or milliseconds e.g. 300ms.
strength
Optional	Sets the strength of the output’s prosodic break by relative terms; possible values are x-weak, weak, medium, strong, and x-strong.
It can be used as shown below:
<Response>
  <Say voice="en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak> Take a deep breath. 
      <break time="200ms"/> exhale. 
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
You can read more about the <break> tag here.
2. <say-as>

Lets you indicate information about the type of text contained and to specify the level of detail for rendering the contained text. It takes the following attributes:
Attribute	Description
interpret-as
Required	determines how the value is spoken; you can get the list of supported values here.
It can be used as shown below:
<Response>
  <Say voice="en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak>There are 
      <say-as interpret-as="cardinal">2006</say-as> people on the waiting list to attend the 
      <say-as interpret-as="ordinal">2</say-as> conference on 
      <say-as interpret-as="characters">CAS</say-as> which will be held on  
      <say-as interpret-as="date" format="yyyymmdd" detail="1">2030-09-04.</say-as>
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
3. <p><s>

These are sentence and paragraph tags:
<Response>
  <Say voice= "en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak>
      <p>
        <s>This is sentence one.</s>
        <s>This is sentence two.</s>
      </p>
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
You can learn more about this tag here.
4. <sub>

Indicate that the text in the alias attribute value replaces the contained text for pronunciation:
<Response>
  <Say voice= "en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak>The 
      <sub alias="World Wide Web">WWW</sub>
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
5. <prosody>

Customizes the pitch, speaking rate, and volume of the text contained by the element:
<Response>
  <Say voice= "en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak>
      <prosody rate="slow" pitch="2st">Custom made sofas.</prosody>
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
You can learn more about this tag here.
6. <emphasis>

Used to add or remove emphasis from text contained by the element. It can take the following attributes:
Attribute	Description
level
Optional	Sets the emphasis level; possible values are strong, moderate, none or reduced.
It can be used as shown below:
<Response>
  <Say voice= "en-US-Wavenet-C">
    <speak>
      <emphasis level="strong">Please call back.</emphasis>
    </speak>
  </Say>
</Response>
You can learn about this tag here.

Copy
<?php
// Save this code in checkBalance.php. Configure the callback URL for your phone number
// to point to the location of this script on the web
// e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/checkBalance.php

// First read in a couple of POST variables passed in with the request

// This is a unique ID generated for this call
$sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];

// Check to see whether this call is active
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {
    // Read in the caller's number. The format will contain the + in the beginning
    $callerNumber = $_POST['callerNumber'];

    // You can replace this array with an actual database table
    $balanceArr = array(
	    '+254711XXXYYY' => 100,
		'+254733YYYZZZ' => 150,
		'+254711000ZZZ' => 190,
	);

    // Read the caller's information from the database if necessary
    if ( array_key_exists($callerNumber, $balanceArr) ) {
        $balance = $balanceArr[$callerNumber];
        $text    = "Your balance is " . $balance . " shillings. Good bye.";
    } else {
        $text = "Sorry, your phone number is not registered for this service. Good Bye.";
    }

    // Compose the response
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Say>'.$text.'</Say>';
    $response .= '</Response>';
      
    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a response in this case

    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];
    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}

Play

This action lets you play back a static audio file that is located anywhere on the web.
<Response>
    <Play url="http://www.myvoicemailserver.com/audio/vmail.wav"/>
</Response>
The Play element can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
url
Required	A valid URL that contains a link to the file to be played. Note that we will cache the content after the first playback request, and will check for request header information that indicates the need to re-download the file later on.

Copy
<?php
// Save this code in voicemail.php. Configure the callback URL for your phone number
// to point to the location of this script on the web
// e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/voicemail.php

// First read in a couple of POST variables passed in with the request

// This is a unique ID generated for this call
$sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];

// Check to see whether this call is active
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {
    // Get the location of previously recorded voicemail and play back the file. Make 
    // sure its a valid web address that starts with http
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Say>Please listen to our awesome record</Say>';
    $response .= '<Play url="http://www.myvoicemailserver.com/audio/vmail.wav"/>';
    $response .= '</Response>';
    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: application/xml');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a response in this case

    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];
    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}

Get Digits

You can use this action to get the digits that a user enters on their phone in response to a prompt from your application. For example, you can ask the user to enter their account number, followed by the hash sign, and then read back their balance to them; to read more about including prompts for inputs, see this
Here is a sample response, with a Say prompt:
<Response>
    <GetDigits timeout="30" finishOnKey="#" callbackUrl="http://mycallbackURL.com">
        <Say>Please enter your account number followed by the hash sign</Say>
    </GetDigits>
</Response>
Once we get this response, our server will read out the text contained in the Say request to the caller and wait for the configured timeout for the response. If the user successfully completed the request and presses the hash sign, our API will forward this response to your web server and fetch the next set of instructions.
Otherwise, if a GetDigits action receives no input at all, it will move on to the next action without triggering a notification. This means that if it is the last action the call will be terminated if the user does not include any input. If you would like us to say something before hanging up, you can add another element after the GetDigits request like this:
<Response>
    <GetDigits timeout="30" finishOnKey="#" callbackUrl="http://mycallbackURL.com">
        <Say>Please enter your account number followed by the hash sign</Say>
    </GetDigits>
    <Say>We did not get your account number. Good bye</Say>
</Response>
The GetDigits action can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
callbackUrl
Optional	The field instructs us to forward the results of the GetDigits action to the URL value passed in. If absent, our API will forward the request to the default URL for this phone number (or to the redirected URL if a redirect has been issued). Default: None
numDigits
Optional	This shows the number of digits you would like to grab from the user input. Default: None
timeout
Optional	Timeout (in seconds) for getting the digits, after which the system moves on to the next element. If there is no other element to execute, the system will hang up. Default: 30 Seconds
finishOnKey
Optional	The key which will terminate the action of getting digits. Default: None

Copy
// Assuming that you have configured the callback URL for your Africa`s Talking Phone Number to point to queryBalance.php. Below is an example of how you would handle an incoming call, check the user`s balance based on their account number and respond with the result:

<?php
    // Save this code in queryBalance.php. Configure the callback URL for your phone number
    // to point to the location of this script on the web
    // e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/queryBalance.php

    // First read in a couple of POST variables passed in with the request

    // This is a unique ID generated for this call
    $sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];

    // Check to see whether this call is active
    $isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

    // The call is active
    if ($isActive == 1)  {
        // This is the First request we are receiving. Prompt for the account number
        // Compose the response
        $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
        $response .= '<Response>';
        $response .= '<GetDigits finishOnKey="#">';
        $response .= '<Say>Please enter your account number followed by the hash sign</Say>';
        $response .= '</GetDigits>';
        $response .= '</Response>';
    }

    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
?>

//The account number will be sent to the Event URL. Assuming you have configured the Event URL to point to getBalance.php. Below is an example of how you would reply with the account balance based on the dtmfDigits recieved

<?php
    // This is the second request from Africa's Talking
    // Save this code in getBalance.php. Configure the events URL for your phone number
    // to point to the location of this script on the web
    // e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/getBalance.php

    // You can replace this array with an actual database table
    $balanceArr = array(
	    '1234' => 100,
		'1235' => 150,
		'1236' => 190,
	);

    // Read the dtmf digits
    $accountNumber = $_POST['dtmfDigits'];

    // Read the account information from the database if necessary
    if ( array_key_exists($accountNumber, $balanceArr) ) {
        $balance = $balanceArr[$accountNumber];
        $text    = "Your balance is " . $balance . " shillings. Good bye.";
    } else {
        $text = "Sorry, we could not find that account number. Good bye";
    }

    // Compose the response
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Say>'.$text.'</Say>';
    $response .= '</Response>';

    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
?>

Dial

You can use this element to connect callers to agents on WebRTC, sip phones or mobile phones. For example, if you use your Africa’s Talking phone number for customer service queries, you can distribute calls received on that phone number to multiple agents.
No action will be executed after this if the call is picked.
<Response>
    <Dial
        phoneNumbers="+254711XXXYYY,+25631XYYZZZZ,test@ke.sip.africastalking.com"
        ringbackTone="http://mymediafile.com/playme.mp3"
        record="true"
        maxDuration="5"
        sequential="true"
    />
</Response>
The Dial element can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
phoneNumbers
Required	A comma separated list of phone numbers (in international format) to call.
record
optional	Record the conversation (true or false). The URL for the recording will be sent to you once the call is complete. Default: false
sequential
optional	If more than one phone number is provided, this determines whether the phone numbers will be dialed one after the other, or whether they will all ring at the same time. If set to true, the numbers will be dialed one after the other.If set to false, they will ring at the same time and will be handled in the order of who picks up first. Default: false.
callerId
optional	This contains the Africa’s Talking number you want to dial out with. It is mainly important when you call using a sip number. If not specified, the number called by the user will be used.
ringbackTone
optional	This contains a URL location of a media playback you would want the user to listen to when the call has been placed before its picked up.
maxDuration
optional	This contains the maximum amount of time in seconds a call should take.

Copy
<?php
// Save this code in customerService.php. Configure the callback URL for your phone number
// to point to the location of this script on the web
// e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/customerService.php

// First read in a couple of POST variables passed in with the request

// This is a unique ID generated for this call
$sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];

// Check to see whether this call is active
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {  
    // Forward by dialing customer service numbers and record the conversation
    // Compose the response
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Dial record="true" sequential="true" phoneNumbers="+254711XXXYYY,+254733YYYZZZ,test@ke.sip.africastalking.com" ringbackTone="http://mymediafile.com/playme.mp3" />';
    $response .= '</Response>';

    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: application/xml');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a response in thie case

    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];
    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // Be sure to read in the URL of the recorded conversation
    $recording    = $_POST['recordingUrl'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}
?>

Record

This element lets you record a call session into an mp3 file that you can then retrieve and play later. Our API supports partial recording or terminal recording. Partial recording is useful where a particular user response is required like while prompting for a name. For terminal recording, the recording starts when the record action is called until the mobile user hangs up.
Partial Recording

A recording stops when finishOnKey button is pressed or maxLength time is reached or the user hangs up. To read more about including prompts for inputs, see this
Here is a sample response:
<Response>
    <Record finishOnKey="#" maxLength="10" trimSilence="true" playBeep="true">
		  <Say>Please tell us your name after the beep.</Say>
	  </Record>
</Response>
When the recording ends, the URL of the recorded file will be sent in the final response from our APIs in a field named recordingUrl. If no file was recorded, this variable will contain an empty string. The call proceeds based on the response to that notification.
Attribute	Description
finishOnKey
Optional	This shows the number of digits you would like to grab from the user input. Default: None
maxLength
Optional	This specifies the maximum amount of time in seconds a recording should take. Default: None
timeout
Optional	This specifies how long to wait until ending the record session after silence is detected. The record session will be ended after time has elapsed. Default: 3600 seconds.
trimSilence
Optional	This is a boolean attribute which specifies whether you want to remove the final parts of a recording where the user was silent. Default: false
playBeep
Optional	This is a boolean attribute which specifies whether the API should play a beep when the recording starts. Default: false
callbackUrl
Optional	This is the URL of the script to process the recording mp3 file sent by the API. If absent, our API will forward the request to the default URL for this phone number. Default: None
Terminal Recording

Terminal recording doesn’t have any attributes. No other action will be executed after.
<Response>
    <Say playBeep="true">Please leave a message after the beep.</Say>
	  <Record />
</Response>
The URL of the recorded file will be sent in the final response from our APIs in a field named recordingUrl. If no file was recorded, this variable will contain an empty string.

Copy
// The example below demoonstrates how to use the  partial recording

<?php
// Save this code in voicemail.php. Configure the callback URL for your phone number
// to point to the location of this script on the web
// e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/voicemail.php

// First read a couple of the POST variables passed in with the request

// This is a unique ID generated for this call
$sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];

// The caller number
$callerPhoneNumber = $_POST['callerNumber'];

// Check to see whether this call is active
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {
    // Inform the caller that while you may not be available at the moment,
    // you will be happy to take a message

    // Compose the response
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Record finishOnKey="#" maxLength="10" trimSilence="true" playBeep="true" callbackUrl="http://www.myawesomesite.com/finalMessage.php">';
    $response .= '<Say>Please leave a message after the tone.</Say>';
    $response .= '</Record>';
    $response .= '</Response>';

    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a response in this case

    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];
    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // Be sure to read in the URL of the recorded conversation
    $recording    = $_POST['recordingUrl'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}
?>

// Once the action is complete, we will send a post request to the 'callbackUrl' added to the Record Action expecting a second action

<?php
$sessionId = $_POST['sessionId'];
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {
    $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
    $response .= '<Response>';
    $response .= '<Say>Thank you for calling. We have saved your audio recording. Goodbye</Say>';
    $response .= '</Response>';

    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a response in this case

    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];

    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // Be sure to read in the URL of the recorded conversation
    $recording    = $_POST['recordingUrl'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}

Enqueue

Enqueuing is passing an incoming call to a queue to be handled later.
<Response>
    <Enqueue name="test" holdMusic="http://www.mymediaserver.com/audio/callWaiting.wav" />
</Response>
The Enqueue action can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
holdMusic
Optional	A valid URL that contains a link to the file to be played while the user is on hold. Note that we will cache the content after the first playback request, and will check for request header information that indicates the need to re-download the file later on. Default: None
name
Optional	You can put a call in a particular queue. eg. support, general, technical. This would help you dequeue the call to a particular person or team. Default: None
Dequeue

Dequeuing is passing the calls enqueued to a separate number so that it can be handled e.g by an agent.
<Response>
    <Dequeue name="test" phoneNumber="+254711082XXX" />
</Response>
The Dequeue action can take these attributes:
Attribute	Description
phoneNumber
Required	The Phone number which users called to join the queue. Our gateway will check to see whether there is anyone in the queue that corresponds to that phone number and connect the two calls. If there is no one in the queue, the gateway just hangs up.
name
Optional	This is the name of the queue you want to dequeue from. Default: None

Copy
<?php
// Save this code in callCenter.php. Configure the callback URL for BOTH phone numbers
// to point to the location of this script on the web
// e.g http://www.myawesomesite.com/callCenter.php

// Check to see whether this call is active
$isActive  = $_POST['isActive'];

if ($isActive == 1)  {
    // Check to see whether this is the enqueue or dequeue Africas Talking phone number    
    $destinationNumber =  $_POST['destinationNumber'];
    
    if ($destinationNumber == '+254711082XXX') {
        // Assuming this is the phone number you have advertised for people that want to
        // join the queue
        $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
        $response .= '<Response>';
        $response .= '<Enqueue url="http://www.mymediaserver.com/audio/callWaiting.wav"/>';
        $response .= '</Response>';
    } else {
        // This must be the phone number that people call to answer these calls. Dequeue
        // by specifying the phone number that adds people to the queue
        $response  = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>';
        $response .= '<Response>';
        $response .= '<Dequeue phoneNumber="+254711082XXX"/>';
        $response .= '</Response>';
    }

    // Print the response onto the page so that our gateway can read it
    header('Content-type: text/plain');
    echo $response;
} else {
    // Read in call details (duration, cost). This flag is set once the call is completed.
    // In this example (enqueue and dequeue), this call will be made twice, when each caller
    // hangs up
    // Note that the gateway does not expect a properly formatted response

    $sessionId    = $_POST['sessionId']; 
    $duration     = $_POST['durationInSeconds'];
    $currencyCode = $_POST['currencyCode'];
    $amount       = $_POST['amount'];

    // You can then store this information in the database for your records
}

Redirect

This action will transfer control of the call to the script whose URL is passed in. This can help you better organize your call handling logic by spreading the logic across multiple scripts.
Any action after Redirect won’t execute since the API will be handling events from the script it was redirected to.
<Response>
    <Redirect>http://www.myotherhandler.com/process.php</Redirect>
</Response>
Once we get this response, our server will generate a POST request to the specified URL and proceed with the call based on the returned XML. The new url will be used as the callback url for the rest of the call.

Reject

This action lets you reject an incoming call. Note that this should be the only element in your response.
<Response>
    <Reject/>
</Response>
Unless you have a valid use case that requires this action, we highly recommend that you play a message to your callers instead of a blanket rejection. For example:

## Claude · 2026-06-09T17:26:57.998Z

# 🎯 I WAS WRONG — Found The Real Bug In The Docs You Just Sent

Read carefully — I missed two critical things AT's docs say plainly:

## 1. The attribute is `callbackUrl` (LOWERCASE b), not `callBackUrl`

From the **Record** docs you sent:

> `callbackUrl` (Optional) — This is the URL of the script to process the recording mp3 file sent by the API.

I had `callBackUrl` (capital B) the whole time. **AT doesn't recognize that attribute and silently ignores it.** That's why every Record callback fell through to the events webhook instead of firing during the call.

## 2. AT DOES support live back-and-forth with Record

From the same docs:

> **"The call proceeds based on the response to that notification."**

And from the Voice Actions overview:

> Note: Any action that takes input from the user such as **Get Digits** and **Record** will **trigger another notification** to your application with those values so we can know what next action to take.

I told you earlier that AT only delivered recordings async via events. **That was wrong.** AT supports the exact interactive pattern you wanted — kid speaks → server responds → kid speaks again → all in one call — we just had the attribute name miscapitalized.

## 3. The docs also show the canonical pattern nests the prompt INSIDE Record

```xml
<Response>
    <Record finishOnKey="#" maxLength="10" trimSilence="true" playBeep="true">
        <Say>Please tell us your name after the beep.</Say>
    </Record>
</Response>
```

Not `<Play>` then separate `<Record>` like I had it. Both might work, but the official example nests them.

Fixing both right now.

# Deep Research: Should Sentry Live On The Sabi-Server (Hetzner Python Box) Too?

## Yes. Here's why and how.

You have **two backends** for Sabi:

| Backend | Where | What runs there | Sentry status now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curriculum-app` (Next.js) | Vercel | Webhook handlers, Claude calls, ElevenLabs proxying, Supabase writes | ✅ Sentry installed today |
| `sabi-server` (Python/FastAPI) | Hetzner 136.243.8.51 | Chatterbox TTS (your voice clone), Whisper STT fallback, the heavy GPU work | ❌ No Sentry |

**Errors on sabi-server are currently invisible.** If Chatterbox crashes mid-synthesis, if Whisper OOMs on a long audio file, if the Hetzner box's CUDA driver hiccups — you have NO way to see it. Curriculum-app's Sentry only catches the Vercel-side request failing, not the upstream cause.

## What Sentry-Python Adds (Real Use Cases For Sabi-Server)

1. **GPU OOM detection** — Chatterbox TTS occasionally OOMs on long sentences. Sentry catches the CUDA error with full Python stack
2. **Slow inference alerts** — Whisper transcription >10s is usually a sign something's wrong. Sentry's performance traces flag the outlier
3. **Voice clone quality drift** — when Chatterbox returns silence or junk audio (the audio buffer is empty), exception → alert
4. **Connection issues from Vercel → Hetzner** — both sides instrumented means a 502 between them gets traced on BOTH sides, with the cause visible in whichever errored first
5. **Distributed tracing** — a single AT call kicks off: Vercel `/incoming` → Anthropic → Hetzner Chatterbox → back to Vercel → Supabase. With Sentry on both, **you see ONE trace spanning ALL of it** — currently you only see the Vercel half

## Setup Cost (Honest)

| Setup item | Time |
|---|---|
| `pip install sentry-sdk[fastapi]` on Hetzner | 1 min |
| Add 8 lines to sabi-server's `main.py` | 2 min |
| Add `SENTRY_DSN` env var (same DSN as curriculum-app or a separate project) | 1 min |
| Configure distributed tracing propagation header forwarding from Next.js | 5 min |
| Test by triggering a deliberate error on Hetzner | 2 min |

**Total: ~10 minutes of work, no extra cost** (the DSN you already paid for handles unlimited projects). If you want them as separate Sentry projects (so dashboards stay clean), the auth token I have can create a new `sabi-server` project via API in seconds.

## Recommended Architecture

```
                   Sentry org "sabi-43"
                   /                 \
   project: javascript-nextjs    project: sabi-server-python
   (curriculum-app on Vercel)     (FastAPI on Hetzner)
        |                                |
        +------ trace_id shared ---------+
        (linked via sentry-trace header)
```

The single trace ID flows through both backends — when you click a failing call in Sentry, you see the WHOLE pipeline in one view, regardless of which box errored.

## Claude · 2026-06-09T20:49:18.948Z

Fixed. **Restart the Antigravity terminal** (close the tab, open a new one — `~/.zshenv` only loads on shell start).

# What I Did

Added two lines to `~/.zshenv` (the file zsh always reads, even in non-interactive IDE terminals):

```bash
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"   # Homebrew paths
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"           # System node/npm install
```

# Verify In Antigravity

1. **Close the current terminal tab** (Cmd+W on the terminal or just open a new one)
2. Open a fresh terminal
3. Run:

```bash
which node     # should show /usr/local/bin/node or /opt/homebrew/bin/node
which npm      # should show /usr/local/bin/npm or /opt/homebrew/bin/npm
node --version # v24.x or v25.x
npm --version  # 11.x
```

# If Still Broken

Antigravity might force its own PATH. Quick override — paste into the Antigravity terminal at the start of the session:

```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
```

Or check Antigravity Settings → Terminal → there might be an "Inherit environment" or "Run as login shell" toggle. Flipping that on usually makes IDE terminals behave like normal terminals.

# Why This Happened

IDE terminals often run zsh **without** the `-l` (login) or `-i` (interactive) flags to speed up startup. That skips `~/.zprofile` (where Homebrew normally lives) and `~/.zshrc` (where your normal PATH gets built). Only `~/.zshenv` runs in all four modes. That's why putting Homebrew there is the bulletproof fix.
